items.q: Is the pack useful if I have debt?
items.a: Debt decisions are part of the book, including Tanya’s composite story. The material is educational and does not replace advice about your individual circumstances.

items.q: Do I need Excel or paid software?
items.a: The workbook is designed for Excel and free Google Sheets. You can print the checklists and keep using the downloadable resources.

items.q: What if my income or situation is different?
items.a: The pack includes sections for tight budgets, higher earners, couples and families, readers 50 and over, and irregular income. The calculators use your own numbers.

items.q: What is different from watching the channel?
items.a: The pack gives you an ordered twelve-chapter path, editable calculators, reusable checklists and scripts in one place. You can return to the tools while working with your own numbers.

items.text: My goodness Alicia. Thank you for this video. I seriously feel like you're directly speaking to me . Im 47, few jobs with saving, but nothing consistent to make a true difference in my retirement account. Now in a new phase of life with a son going to college im still working, felt somewhat defeated and overwhelmed, however this video here gives me HOPE with a gps. Love all the examples. Helps me to see myself in another light.  Bookmarking so I can always listen to as a reminder. You're awesome!
items.video: The Proven Path From Broke to Quiet Millionaire (If You're Behind, Watch This!)

items.text:
Hello Alicia. I’m commenting from Lagos, Nigeria. 

I’ve been binge-watching most of your videos and would like to tell you that they have been very helpful and impactful. 

I’m halfway through the mark and very confident that before the year runs out, I will have reached the finish line. When you said that “idle money” helps you create calm, steadiness and a spine, I felt it. I hollered because that’s what’s happening to me too. I have become much more disciplined with my finances that my friends have set up a speaking engagement this month for me to come talk about it. I’m excited to share all I’ve learnt and looking forward to it. IMAGINE ME!!

Your work on here is relevant. Please don’t stop and God bless you real good.
items.video: How I Built a Full Year of Emergency Savings on a $30,000 Salary (The Exact System)

items.text: Really appreciate this video. It helped me realize I’m currently doing better than I thought, even when it feels like I’m behind. It also helped me reframe how I feel about my past choices between the ages of 18 and 30 (The guilt is real!). Many of those choices were about survival, limited financial literacy, and earning power while putting myself through college and paying rent, not failure (i.e., depending on credit cards to buy groceries and other necessities)!  Also, thank you for making the point about not comparing finances and lifestyles with others who appear to be better off than you- so true!
items.video: What You Should Have Accomplished by 40 | How to Catch Up Fast

items.text: I love your channel! Your Alicia character and presentation is a winner, Excellent info on personal finance, accessible to everybody.. You could branch out into other topics, with Alicia starring in each. Cooking, relationships, home maintenance,  job search, navigating university, de-cluttering a home, caring for aging parents, pet care, health care, insurance policies, whatever. We'd all tune in to hear Alicia. Looking forward to much more.

items.text: I recently called a repairman to service my refrigerator instead of running out to buy another refrigerator. Its sealant was replaced. Plus I asked a lot of questions about appliances they repair often so he told me what not to buy. 👍🏾 This was due to me watching your videos. Plus just planted a few vegetables yesterday. items.text: I think that you, Alicia, should make a series of financial lesson videos for students, from basic lessons for elementary and middle school students on wants vs. needs, etc., to more advanced lessons for high schoolers, and especially for young people about to launch into the world of work or college. You explain and illustrate things so clearly for adults. A step by step curriculum for young people would be something I would love to share with people in my life. BTW, I was a teacher before I retired, and the best teachers always shared life lessons with students, no matter which subjects we taught.

items.text:
I realized I am already rich! 😊
I do all of them currently successfully or progressively. When I tell people I leave my personal cell phone in the office downstairs, they think I’m crazy and that it is unsafe. Well I do it for the sake of peace of mind and mental health. That’s safe to me. 
The ones that are still hard for me is to say no to my closed circle … yeah this is hard on me. But I will keep trying. And I would love to stay away from my phone more often. 

Thanks for this. I really appreciate this video!

checkup.heading: Where are you right now?
checkup.intro: Eight quick questions. There are no wrong answers, and nothing you choose leaves this page. At the end you get a short plan you can keep.
checkup.aliciaNote: Answer the way things are, not the way you wish they were. That’s where a good plan starts.
checkup.chaptersTitle: Where I’d start in the Playbook
checkup.disclaimer: A starting point for learning, based on your answers. Not personal financial advice.
checkup.noJs: The check-up needs JavaScript to work. You can still open the free printable worksheet.

questions.q: When you check your bank balance, how do you usually feel?
Do you know roughly what your regular bills add up to each month?
If a $500 surprise bill arrived tomorrow, you would…
options: Put it on a card or borrow
Pay it, but it would hurt
Take it from money set aside

questions.q: How well do you know your subscriptions and memberships?
Apart from a mortgage, how does debt feel right now?

options: It comes in and goes out
Bills get paid, the rest drifts

questions.q: Is there a big money decision coming in the next year?
options: Asking for a raise or a new job

questions.q: Which sounds most like your life right now?

fog: Before any plan, it helps to see clearly. Your first job is simply to know where the money goes. That alone takes a lot of the worry out of it.
cushion: You know your numbers. The next layer is a buffer, so a surprise bill becomes an inconvenience instead of an emergency.
rhythm: The basics are there. What would help most now is a simple system, so the right things happen on payday without you having to think about them.
ahead: Your foundations look steady. This is a good moment to learn the next steps calmly, at your own pace.

steps.look: Look at your balance once this week, just to look. No decisions needed.
steps.list: Add up your regular bills for one month. A rough number is fine.
steps.subs: List your subscriptions and memberships. The Leak Hunt on this page can help.
steps.cushion: Choose a first cushion target, even $500, and give it its own account.
steps.debt: Write each debt on one page with its balance, rate and minimum payment.
steps.payday: Decide what happens on payday: bills first, then a set amount to savings, then spending.
steps.car: Before the car decision, add up the full yearly cost: payment, insurance, fuel and repairs.
steps.home: Before the home decision, list the costs beyond the mortgage: taxes, insurance, repairs and upkeep.
steps.celebration: Set the number you’re comfortable with before the planning starts.
steps.raise: Write down three things you’ve done this year that show the value of your work.
steps.moneydate: Set a monthly money date to look at where things stand.
steps.learn: Learn the basics of investing before choosing anything. Take it slowly.

leakHunt.heading: Let’s find the quiet leaks.
leakHunt.intro: Tap the costs you pay for, then change the amounts to match your own bills. You’ll see what they add up to in a year, and decide what to keep, ask about or cancel.
leakHunt.exampleNote: Example list to start with. Tap any cost to add or remove it, and change the amounts to match your bills.
leakHunt.hours: About {hours} hours of work a year
leakHunt.note: Amounts to look at, not a promise of savings.
leakHunt.planEmpty: Mark a cost as Ask about or Cancel and your action list appears here.
leakHunt.callScript: Hello. I’m reviewing my {name} bill. Could you explain my current plan, any extra fees and the lower-cost options available? Before I change anything, please confirm the total price, what I would lose and whether there is a contract or cancellation fee.
leakHunt.cancelSteps: Check the terms and the last billing date, cancel, and keep the confirmation.
leakHunt.downloadStatus: Spreadsheet prepared. Open it in Excel or import it into Google Sheets.
leakHunt.empty: Add a cost you recognize and I’ll add up the year with you.
leakHunt.noJs: The Leak Hunt needs JavaScript to work. You can still open the free printable worksheet.
